system.name: JANUS
system.one_liner: a cross-world, cooperative nested-virtualization hypervisor design that secures containers with efficient three-level address translation

components.name: Guest root PGD
components.role: L2 guest's top-level page table, constructed on demand with read-write EPT0→2 mappings

components.name: Guest PTE
components.role: L2 guest's page table entries, mapping to the read-write L2 Page

components.name: Shadow Root
components.role: a shadow PGD mirroring the real GPT_L2, pre-mapped read-only in EPT0→2 to block unauthorized modification

components.name: Switcher PUD
components.role: shadow PUD level installed by L1 to reference the switcher's tables

components.name: Switcher PMD
components.role: shadow PMD level of the switcher's page tables

components.name: Switcher PTE
components.role: shadow PTE level, mapping to the read-only L1 Page

components.name: L2_Page
components.role: the read-write page reachable through the guest's real page-table chain

components.name: L1_Page
components.role: the read-only page reachable through the shadow root's page-table chain

content.key_idea: JANUS mirrors the real L2 guest page global directory into a hardware-protected, read-only shadow root so a compromised L2 kernel cannot remap or overwrite the world-switcher, forwarding only L1-validated PGD updates to the hardware MMU.
content.reading_order: Two aligned rows, left to right (root/PGD to PTE): L2 Kernel's guest chain on top, CR3-rooted shadow chain below, linked by vertical sync arrows per column.

summary: This figure explains JANUS's shadow-root integrity mechanism for its world switcher. It draws two parallel page-table chains from root to leaf (PGD/PUD/PMD/PTE): on top, the L2 Kernel's real guest page tables (Guest root PGD through Guest PTE), constructed on demand with read-write EPT0→2 mappings down to an L2 Page; on the bottom, a CR3-rooted Shadow Root and its Switcher PUD/PMD/PTE levels, pre-mapped read-only in EPT0→2 and always present, reaching a separate L1 Page. Vertical arrows tie each column together, showing that an L2 attempt to modify a PGD entry must go through an L1-validated hypercall that updates the shadow root before the change is visible to hardware, while lower-level PUD/PMD/PTE edits proceed without L1 involvement. A dashed line separates the read-write guest-page region from the read-only shadow-page region.
summary_zh: 图7展示JANUS影子根机制:上方为L2真实页表链(按需构建,读写),下方为CR3影子页表链(只读且始终存在),两链逐级对应连接,虚线分隔RW的L2页与RO的L1页,防止恶意L2篡改switcher。
notes: layout-proposal: mirrored page-table chains — two parallel guest/shadow page-table walks (root through PTE) aligned column by column with vertical sync/mapping arrows between corresponding levels; matrix is the closest named template for the row/column grid, but the figure's real point is the top/bottom mirroring and RW/RO contrast rather than an independent two-axis comparison.
